entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Boehnhardt et al. (2002), A&A 387, 1107); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Wirtanen was Rosetta’s planned destination before a launch delay changed the mission’s target to 67P. Its small nucleus returns to the inner Solar System roughly every five years. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Boehnhardt et al. (2002), A&A 387, 1107: effective radius 0.6 km. Lightcurves give an axis ratio of at least 1.4 and a period of 6 to 7.5 hours; the minimum elongation is displayed. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
